phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Analyzed distributed blob publishing atomicity guarantees during EL communication failures. Identified critical state-space anomalies where partial data column publication can occur without rollback mechanisms, creating inconsistent availability states across the network.

call_flow: 3. DataColumnSidecars() constructs columns from EL response

anomalies.description: GetBlobsV2 can return partial results if EL communication fails mid-transfer
Empty array could mean: (1) no blobs available, (2) network failure, (3) timeout
anomalies.impact: Cannot distinguish between legitimate empty state and failure state

abstract_domain.cardinality: expected: 0 OR 128; actual: can be any value in [0, 128]

anomalies.description: If GetBlobsV2 returns partial data, DataColumnSidecars() will construct only available columns
anomalies.impact: Network sees incomplete column set without knowing if more are coming

anomalies.description: Code expects 0 or 128 columns (line 243-244) but can receive any count in [1, 127]
anomalies.impact: Boundary check only validates on subsequent calls, first partial result goes unchecked

abstract_domain.semantic: tracks which column indices were newly broadcast

anomalies.description: Each retry can broadcast additional columns without tracking global completion state
anomalies.impact: Network may never know if full 128 columns were intended or if process was interrupted

anomalies.description: DataColumnStorage.Save() appends incrementally without transaction or savepoint mechanism
anomalies.impact: If process crashes during Save(), partial columns are persisted without metadata indicating incompleteness

anomalies.description: file.Sync() at line 802-804 commits whatever was written, even if not all 128 columns
anomalies.impact: Filesystem reflects partial state as if it were a complete, valid state

anomalies.description: No maximum retry limit, only exits when context cancelled or all columns seen
anomalies.impact: Can retry indefinitely if EL persistently returns partial data, accumulating partial publishes

anomalies.description: 250ms delay per iteration (line 269) without exponential backoff
anomalies.impact: Fast retry loop may not give EL time to recover, causing repeated partial fetches

anomalies.description: Indices header updated separately from column data (lines 784-790, 793-799)
anomalies.impact: If crash occurs between header update and data write, file metadata claims more columns than actually stored

anomalies.description: storageIndices tracks count but doesn't enforce 0 or 128 invariant at storage layer
anomalies.impact: Partial column sets are valid at filesystem level, contradicting protocol assumptions

abstract_domain.semantic: P2P message accumulator for batch publishing

anomalies.description: Batch publish can fail after some messages sent but before all sent
anomalies.impact: Some subnets receive columns, others don't - creates partitioned view across network

anomalies.description: BroadcastDataColumnSidecars is non-blocking (line 356: go s.broadcastDataColumnSidecars), no status returned
anomalies.impact: Caller cannot know if broadcast succeeded, failed, or partially succeeded

state_anomalies_found.description: Distributed blob publishing lacks atomicity guarantee - partial data column sets can be published to the network without a mechanism to rollback or signal incompleteness

intermediate_states: S1 = GetBlobsV2() → {blobs: [b0, b1], columns: ∅, published: ∅}  [partial fetch from EL]
S2 = ConstructDataColumns() → {blobs: [b0, b1], columns: [c0..c31], published: ∅}  [only 32 of 128 columns]
S3 = BroadcastDataColumns() → {blobs: [b0, b1], columns: [c0..c31], published: [c0..c31]}  [partial publish]
S4 = DataColumnStorage.Save() → {blobs: [b0, b1], columns: [c0..c31], published: [c0..c31], stored: [c0..c31]}  [partial persist]
abstract_interpretation_evidence.failure_state: SF = {network_timeout: true, rollback: NONE, state: S4}  [partial data permanently visible]
abstract_interpretation_evidence.expected_final_state: SE = {blobs: [all], columns: [c0..c127], published: [c0..c127], stored: [c0..c127]} OR {blobs: ∅, columns: ∅, published: ∅, stored: ∅}
abstract_interpretation_evidence.actual_final_state_range: SA ∈ [S0, SE] with no guarantee of reaching SE

violation_points: GetBlobsV2 can return partial results (no EL-level atomicity)
Retry loop adds more columns without checking if initial set was complete

network_impact.da_layer: Partial columns published create ambiguous data availability state
network_impact.peer_view: Different peers may see different column subsets depending on when they queried
network_impact.reconstruction: Nodes attempting reconstruction may fail if they cached partial state before completion
network_impact.time_window: Between first partial publish and eventual completion (or abandonment), network state is inconsistent

state_anomalies_found.description: Race condition between checking if columns are seen (line 296) and broadcasting them (line 310) - columns may arrive from peers during this window

abstract_interpretation_evidence.race_condition: If peer broadcasts same column during Δ(T0, T1), duplicate broadcast occurs

state_anomalies_found.impact: Duplicate columns broadcast to network, wasting bandwidth and potentially creating ambiguity about intended column set

state_anomalies_found.description: Infinite retry loop without maximum iteration bound can lead to unbounded state accumulation if EL persistently returns partial data

abstract_interpretation_evidence.non_termination_scenario: If GetBlobsV2 always returns empty array AND not all columns seen, loop never exits
abstract_interpretation_evidence.state_growth: Each iteration: 1 metric increment, 1 log entry, 250ms delay - unbounded accumulation

state_anomalies_found.impact: Resource exhaustion through log spam, metric inflation, and goroutine retention if many blocks trigger this path simultaneously

state_anomalies_found.description: Filesystem metadata (indices header) is written separately from column data, creating window where metadata claims more columns exist than are actually stored
state_anomalies_found.impact: If crash occurs in crash window, file metadata claims columns that don't exist, causing read failures or incorrect data availability signals

state_anomalies_found.description: GetBlobsV2 returning empty array has three distinct semantic meanings that are indistinguishable to the caller

semantic_interpretations: LEGITIMATE_EMPTY: No blobs exist for these versioned hashes (blocks with zero blobs)
NETWORK_FAILURE: RPC call failed mid-response, returned partial empty data
TIMEOUT: Request timed out before EL could respond, returned default empty array
NOT_READY: EL has blobs but hasn't computed cells/proofs yet (spec allows lazy computation)
abstract_interpretation_evidence.caller_action: Lines 742-743 treat all as 'no data available', return early without distinguishing

code_locations: subscriber_beacon_blocks.go:239-240 (retry logic assumes empty = try again later)
state_anomalies_found.impact: Legitimate zero-blob blocks are retried unnecessarily; network failures are not logged as errors; no way to detect EL cells/proofs computation delays

state_anomalies_found.description: P2P batch broadcast can fail after some messages are sent but before all are sent, with no rollback or retry of the failed subset

abstract_interpretation_evidence.no_retry_mechanism: broadcaster.go:416-420 only logs error, doesn't retry failed subset

state_anomalies_found.impact: Network sees partial column set on some subnets but not others, creating partitioned data availability view; no mechanism to detect or correct this divergence

critical_findings.description: No code path exists to rollback partial column publications if EL communication fails mid-process
evidence: DataColumnStorage.Save() is append-only with no delete/rollback API
BroadcastDataColumnSidecars() is fire-and-forget with no cancellation mechanism
Retry loop only adds more columns, never removes already-published partial sets

critical_findings.description: Network has no way to know if a column set is complete or still being published incrementally
evidence: DataColumnStorageSummary only tracks 'which indices exist', not 'are all expected indices present'
No protocol-level signal indicating 'publication complete' vs 'publication in progress'
Peers must assume partial set is incomplete and wait, but no timeout or completion guarantee

critical_findings.description: Broadcast returns immediately without waiting for P2P confirmation, making failure detection impossible
evidence: broadcaster.go:356 launches goroutine with 'go s.broadcastDataColumnSidecars(ctx, forkDigest, sidecars)'
No channel or callback to signal broadcast completion or failure

critical_findings.description: Filesystem storage accumulates columns incrementally without ACID transaction guarantees
evidence: data_column.go:783-799 writes header, then data, without single atomic operation
data_column.go:802 file.Sync() commits whatever was written, even if incomplete
No rollback if process crashes between header and data writes

recommendations.recommendation: Implement two-phase commit protocol for distributed blob publishing
recommendations.rationale: Atomicity requires coordination between EL fetch, local storage, and P2P broadcast
implementation_approach: Phase 1 (Prepare): Fetch all blobs/cells from EL, validate count == 128 or 0, store in temp location
Phase 2 (Commit): Only if Phase 1 fully succeeds, atomically rename temp → final, then broadcast all
Rollback: If any step fails, delete temp storage and abort broadcast

recommendations.rationale: Network needs to distinguish 'partial set still being built' from 'complete set published'
implementation_approach: Add 'completion_status' field to file header: PARTIAL | COMPLETE
Only mark COMPLETE when count == 128 AND all indices [0..127] are present
Expose via DataColumnStorageSummary.IsComplete() API
Peers should wait for IsComplete() before trusting data availability

recommendations.recommendation: Make BroadcastDataColumnSidecars synchronous with error reporting
recommendations.rationale: Caller needs to know if broadcast succeeded to decide whether to retry or rollback
implementation_approach: Change signature to return error channel: BroadcastDataColumnSidecars(...) <-chan error
Wait for all subnet publishes to complete or fail
Return aggregated error indicating which subnets failed
Caller can retry failed subnets or rollback entire publication

recommendations.recommendation: Add maximum retry limit to processDataColumnSidecarsFromExecution
recommendations.rationale: Unbounded retry can cause resource exhaustion if EL is persistently failing
implementation_approach: const maxRetries = 10 (or configuration parameter)
Track iteration count and exit loop if iteration >= maxRetries
Log error and emit metric when max retries exceeded
Consider exponential backoff: delay = 250ms * (2 ** min(iteration, 5))

recommendations.recommendation: Add GetBlobsV2 response validation to distinguish empty states
recommendations.rationale: Empty response should be validated against expected blob count from block commitments
implementation_approach: Compare len(blobAndProofV2s) with len(kzgCommitments)
If mismatch and len(blobAndProofV2s) == 0, treat as EL error, not 'no blobs'
Add RPC error code inspection to distinguish timeout vs not-found
Only retry on timeout/transient errors, fail fast on permanent errors

recommendations.recommendation: Implement atomic file write with rename for DataColumnStorage
recommendations.rationale: Prevent metadata/data incoherence if crash occurs during write
implementation_approach: Write to temporary file (e.g., <blockroot>.tmp.sszs)
Write header and all data to temp file
Sync temp file
Atomically rename temp → final (OS guarantees atomic rename)
This ensures file is either fully written or doesn't exist

test_scenarios.scenario: EL timeout during GetBlobsV2 after partial response
test_scenarios.setup: Mock EL to send first 2 BlobAndProofV2 objects, then timeout
test_scenarios.expected_behavior: System should detect partial response, not publish any columns, retry full request
test_scenarios.actual_behavior: Partial columns constructed and published, retry adds more columns incrementally

test_scenarios.scenario: Process crash between header write and data write
test_scenarios.setup: Inject crash signal after data_column.go:790, before line 793
test_scenarios.expected_behavior: On restart, file should be detected as corrupt/incomplete and ignored or repaired
test_scenarios.actual_behavior: File appears valid with metadata claiming columns that don't exist, causes read errors

test_scenarios.scenario: P2P batch publish fails after 50% messages sent
test_scenarios.setup: Mock pubsub to succeed on first 64 messages, fail on remaining 64
test_scenarios.expected_behavior: Broadcast should rollback or retry failed subset, or fail entirely atomically
test_scenarios.actual_behavior: First 64 columns broadcast to network, last 64 lost, no retry or error to caller

test_scenarios.scenario: Concurrent GetBlobsV2 requests for same block root
test_scenarios.setup: Two goroutines call ConstructDataColumnSidecars for same block simultaneously
test_scenarios.expected_behavior: Single flight mechanism should deduplicate, only one EL request made
test_scenarios.actual_behavior: columnSidecarsExecSingleFlight deduplicates correctly, but both goroutines may publish, wasting resources

test_scenarios.scenario: Infinite retry loop with EL always returning empty
test_scenarios.setup: Mock EL to always return empty array for GetBlobsV2, never set all columns as 'seen'
test_scenarios.expected_behavior: After max retries, should fail with error, not loop forever
test_scenarios.actual_behavior: Loops forever until context cancelled, consuming resources
